name: Layered cutout characters
oneLiner: HD painted characters built from cut-out parts and moved by a small bone rig in code instead of frame-by-frame drawing: each original character is generated once as a full body and then as a parts sheet (head, torso, hips, upper / lower arms, thighs, shins, weapon, shield, cape or coat skirt), cut and packed into one atlas + rig by a script; the module gives a breathing idle, a walk cycle with planted feet, an overhead attack and a forward slash with anticipation, strike and recover, a blade swoosh, a crisp hit flash, hurt recoil, guard, cheer, cast, jump and fall, feet planted by IK, a spring cape, a code key light with a warm rim, and draws at device resolution. The game's own timers drive it; its rules never change.
fits: side-scrolling action and platformers with a hero and a few humanoid foes
turn-based, tactics and squad battles shown in side view (attack, hurt, guard, victory poses)
dialogue or story scenes with full-body characters standing on a stage
any HD game that wants hand-painted characters that move smoothly without sprite sheets
notFor: pixel-art styles on a fixed low-resolution canvas (pixel8, pixel16, handheld4): the painted HD art clashes
top-down or front-facing characters (the parts are painted in a three-quarter side view facing right; left is a mirror)
non-humanoid creatures (the rig is a biped; a beast needs its own rig)
art generated at runtime (the game only loads files)

needs: the draw site of each replaced character: feet point, drawn height, facing, hit flash and blink
the character's states from the game's fixed step: attack timer and length, hurt timer, airborne, running speed
the game's boot moved into onReady (atlases loaded before the first step)
the pack: pack.js (or pack.json) + chars/<id>.webp, or the designer's own pack made with the regenerate prompt
provides: actor.draw(ctx, feetX, feetY, {h, facing, flash, alpha, light}) -> bool: the painted, posed character (false = not loaded, keep the old drawing)
actor.pose(anim, k) / play(anim, {dur, onHit}) / loop(anim): idle, walk, attack, cast, hurt, guard, cheer, jump, down
lib.walkSpeed(id) (no foot sliding), lib.drawHead(ctx, id, x, y, r) (portrait / turn-order heads), flash: 'auto', swoosh
lib.drawPose(ctx, id, x, footY, {pose, k, t, fall}): stateless drawing for hosts that compute poses (squad clash)

checks/run-checks.py joins: every animation sample at 2x with a per-part ID buffer; fails on a floating part, an item not held or a visible joint stub; neck: head pivot on the neck, neck length, head : body ratio, neck stub hidden, no seam at the collar
actor.point('tip' | 'hand' | 'head'): where the weapon tip etc. is drawn now
tools/make-pack.py: parts sheet -> atlas + rig (pivots, joints, z order), sleeve stubs cut away (erase) and joint stubs listed (pegs), foot split at the ankle, overlay check
assets.json manifest with every image_gen call (savedPath, revisedPrompt, input sha256), atlas sha256, source sheets

promptParams.default: the player character (plus any ally or enemy one of the pack's characters fits)

assets: module/cutout-characters.js: the rig, animation sets and renderer (global GameDNA_Cutout)
assets/pack.js + pack.json: rigs of 3 characters (sword, spear, mage); assets/chars/*.webp: one atlas each (182 KB total)
assets/assets.json: manifest (4 image_gen calls: style mother line-up + 3 parts sheets; savedPath, revisedPrompt, input sha256; atlas sha256)
assets/prompts/: style-lock.txt (words only), templates.md (full body, parts sheet, rig config), the briefs actually sent
tools/make-pack.py (cut, alpha, scale, foot split, pack, overlay) and tools/make-manifest.py; shared tools/assets (gen.sh, genmeta.py, namecheck.py, postproc.py, assetcheck.py)

assetPack.check: tools/assets/assetcheck.py assets/assets.json; checks/run-checks.py (rig, limits, joint gaps, determinism, perf)
assetPack.regenerate: prompt.md (Regenerate) + assets/prompts/templates.md + style-lock.txt + assets/rig-config.json + tools/make-pack.py + tools/assets

related.art-direction-lock: L-00: the style-lock method (one STYLE LOCK paragraph in every prompt, the first image as the reference for the rest)
related.squad-clash: A-14: drawUnit hook -> lib.drawPose with the clash's pose, k, t and fall, drawn at 1.1x the built-in height; turn-order heads through a drawHead hook (checks/hosts/squad-clash)
related.normal-maps: L-05 lights flat sprites; this element lights its layer with a code key light and rim instead (the parts carry baked light)
related.hit-sparks: E-02 / E-11: place sparks at actor.point('tip')
